Hi Alex / Maya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to see the demo translated into a couple of concrete integration paths. Per our conversation, I attached two artifacts: a one-page POCTerms draft and an example workbook that shows what an ops-credit smoothing path looks like over a 30-day timebox.

Quick summary of the two approaches we discussed:
- Short extension (7–14 days): extends the timebox, flat additional days, single amendment.
- Credit smoothing (credit buckets): keep end date, allocate ops credits that release over the remaining term so you avoid a big upfront invoice.

If I had to call out tradeoffs: extension gives you more calendar time to run experiments but pushes procurement to approve an addendum; smoothing keeps procurement flow simpler but is a billing/credit construct that Finance will need to accept.

Can you tell me which you prefer? If smoothing, I can propose 2 variants (aggressive vs. conservative) with explicit token/hours equivalence so Finance can validate.

I copied a couple folks on my side to advise on revenue/ops impact. If you want, we can fast-track a short amendment via DocuSign once you pick an option.

Thanks —

Thanks for the context. Quick proposal below — I recommend we offer Option B as a standard for SM mid-market pilots where procurement is the choke point.

Options (numbers use the example workbook assumptions):

- Option A — Short extension (10 days)
  - Adds 10 calendar days to pilot; one amendment; no change to unit price.
  - Revenue impact: +10% run-rate for the quarter compared to baseline.
  - Legal: simple amendment, sign + DocuSign.

- Option B — Weekly credit smoothing (RECOMMENDED)
  - Keep current end date; create a 4-week credit bucket that pays out weekly. Example: total ops credit = 120k token-equivalent (from workbook) split into 4 releases of 30k each.
  - Price protection: hold the quoted committed rate for 30 days after the pilot if the customer converts to a committed plan.
  - Revenue impact: recognized as deferred revenue until credits consumed; lower near-term cash but preserves momentum.
  - Finance/legal: need a short Addendum + statement of credit schedule (we have templates).

- Option C — Conditional conversion voucher
  - Offer smaller immediate credit + a conversion voucher that provides a discount on first 3 months if they commit.
  - Best if they need extra incentives to close.

Operational notes:
- We should include clear token-hour equivalence per bucket in the DocuSign amendment.
- If they ask for weekly releases, our billing can auto-apply credits at the weekly cadence — engineering/ops already supports that workflow.
- Recommend disabling auto-overage to avoid surprise invoices; overage can be converted to pay-as-you-go at quoted rate.

I'll draft the language for Option B and run it by Legal (David) today — David, can you confirm the 30-day price-protection phrasing is OK? If yes, Steph — we can turn this into a DocuSign in <24 hours.

— Marcus Lin
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
